TiSASRec distinguishes sequence position from pairwise elapsed time: r_ij=min(k,⌊|T_i−T_j|/r_min,u⌋), attention logits e_ij=q_i·(k_j+r^K_ij+p^K_j)/√d, and output z_i=Σ_j softmax(e_ij)(v_j+r^V_ij+p^V_j). Temporal embeddings are learned, not necessarily monotone decay. Table 5 compares position-only SASRec, interval-only TiSASRec-R, and both: combined performs best across six datasets; interval-only sometimes loses to SASRec, especially with identical timestamps. [Original paper](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf).

Exponential history pooling h=Σ_i exp(−(T−T_i)/ρ)e_i, optionally normalized, measures individual event recency. Pairwise distance |T_i−T_j| instead measures separation, regardless of whether both events are ancient. MEANTIME explicitly encodes exp(−|d_ij|/freq^(c/h)), with d_ij=(T_i−T_j)/τ, alongside sinusoidal/logarithmic kernels. Its fixed-dimension embedding-combination ablations find dataset-dependent benefits; they do not establish recurring-interest freshness. [Equations 1–2, §4.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2008.08273).

Algebraic diagnosis of the proposed operator: t−max(i,j) is age of the later endpoint, not pairwise distance. If witnesses satisfy j≤i, weights collapse exactly to exp(−(t−i)/ρ_eff)max_j S(i,j), with 1/ρ_eff=1/ρ_anchor+1/ρ_witness: stronger anchor recency. Later witnesses can refresh older anchors, but only if similarity identifies recurrence. Exclude self-witnesses; use observed-prefix events only. Proposed controls: independently tuned anchor-only decay; static max-similarity gating; pair-distance decay; witness-only freshness; shuffled similarities preserving timestamps; and matched residual scale/normalization. Compare macro validation HR@10 under equal tuning budgets. If i,j,t denote positions, the operator measures interaction-count freshness rather than elapsed-time freshness.
